correctness.rationale: The universal radius and center locus follow from exact support-functional norms of coordinate restrictions; reflection+convexity proves that centering a ball at zero loses nothing. Generic dimension is rank of two independent linear constraints. Uniform spherical normal squares have the Dirichlet(1/2) density, yielding the exact scaled-simplex integral; asymptotic constants follow from spherical-coordinate densities and a uniform simplex limit. The minimum of n half-normal variables and a chi-square normalization give the n³ squared-exponential limit; a uniform exponential tail on n^{3/2} minimum coordinate proves convergence of all positive moments. A standalone checker reconstructed 400 literal 3-cube section polygons, compared 2D integration, and sampled finite/asymptotic laws, successfully executing on the embedded package. Finite diagnostics are support only, not a proof of all dimensions.

value.rationale: The inradius is a natural intrinsic metric of Haar cube sections, different from the extensively studied outer radius and face counts. This complete sharp result supplies a fixed-dimensional probability law, two qualitatively different endpoint exponents, full locus of all maximizing centers, and a surprising cubic-scale, non-Gaussian asymptotic law with convergence of every positive moment. These details give a useful precise benchmark for random-section geometry without relying on a speculative general theorem.
